name: Faiss
tagline: Meta's C++/Python library for fast dense-vector similarity search and clustering, CPU and GPU.
description: Faiss is the reference library for approximate nearest neighbour search, developed by Meta's FAIR lab since 2017. It provides a toolkit of index types (flat, IVF, HNSW, PQ/OPQ, scalar and additive quantizers, binary) that can be composed via index factory strings, plus GPU implementations including NVIDIA cuVS integration for billion-scale batch search. It is a library, not a database: there is no server, no metadata store and no durability beyond writing index files. Many vector databases and research systems use Faiss internally or benchmark against it.

scale.notes: Billion-vector indexes on a single GPU server are documented; distribution across machines is up to the application.

strengths: Widest range of ANN index and quantization algorithms in one library
State-of-the-art GPU search, including cuVS integration
Composable index factory for quick experimentation
Battle-tested at Meta scale and in countless research papers
weaknesses: No metadata filtering, persistence layer or server
Deletes and updates are awkward for many index types
Choosing and tuning index types needs expertise
Scaling beyond one machine is your problem
useCases: Embedding similarity search inside ML pipelines
notIdealFor: Applications needing a database with CRUD and filters
Multi-tenant production services without extra infrastructure
